items.title: Groen accepts nuclear energy as possible transition technology
items.headline: Groen party members vote to accept nuclear energy as a transition to renewables.
items.summary: At its congress 'Over Hoop' in Antwerp, Groen members approved a proposal to no longer exclude nuclear energy as a transition technology towards fully renewable energy. The proposal was approved with 70% of votes. The ultimate goal remains an energy supply that is 100% renewable.
items.interest_reason: Significant Belgian energy policy shift; reader follows energy policy.

items.title: Pidpa temporarily replaces digital water meters in 500 homes due to battery drain
items.headline: Pidpa swaps digital water meters for analog in 500 homes over moisture battery drain.
items.summary: Drinkwatermaatschappij Pidpa has temporarily replaced digital water meters with analog ones in about 500 homes. In exceptionally humid conditions, the battery of the digital meter can drain faster, Gazet van Antwerpen reported and VRT NWS confirmed.
items.interest_reason: Utility technical issue, moderate relevance to environment readers.

items.title: Brasschaat introduces immediate fines up to €500 for littering
items.headline: Brasschaat imposes immediate GAS fines up to €500 for littering.
items.summary: The municipality of Brasschaat will immediately fine anyone caught leaving waste next to a bin or on the street with a GAS fine of up to €500. 'The time for awareness and warnings is over,' the municipality said.
items.interest_reason: Local litter enforcement, low policy significance for energy/environment.

items.title: Brussels parliament approves zero-emission requirement for new taxis from 2027
items.headline: Brussels mandates new taxis be zero-emission from January 2027, existing diesels exempt.
items.summary: The Brussels parliament approved an ordinance on Friday confirming the electrification of the Brussels taxi fleet. From 1 January 2027, every newly registered taxi in Brussels must be a zero-emission vehicle. Existing diesel taxis may continue to operate longer.
items.interest_reason: Regional electrification policy, relevant to energy and environment reader.

items.title: COP31 talks in Antalya collapse over fossil fuel wording
items.headline: Antalya climate talks end without a deal as the EU objects to fossil fuel and carbon capture wording.
items.summary: Carbon Pulse reported that COP31 negotiations in Antalya were teetering on collapse on day 13, with the EU walking out and refusing to accept the current cover decision text. The plenary ran into a marathon session and, according to Carbon Pulse's update, countries failed to agree a political deal on Sunday. Vulnerable developing countries joined the EU in objecting to the absence of fossil fuel commitments and the inclusion of carbon capture ambitions.
items.interest_reason: Major EU climate diplomacy outcome; relevant to EU energy and climate policy.

items.title: Firewood prices rise as winter heating costs climb
items.headline: Firewood prices have risen as households turn to wood heating amid higher oil and gas costs.
items.summary: Tagesspiegel reports that heating with wood has become more expensive as winter approaches. The article attributes the pressure to oil and gas prices that have risen sharply due to international crises. The candidate text gives no specific figures for wood prices, so the detail beyond the headline is limited.
items.interest_reason: Consumer heating-cost story; no profile basis, limited energy policy substance.

items.title: Nine Liège-province municipalities begin sharing electricity, a first in Wallonia
items.headline: Nine municipalities in Liège province now share their electricity, the first such arrangement in Wallonia.
items.summary: According to RTBF Info, nine communes in the province of Liège are sharing their electricity, which is described as a first in Wallonia. The report's opening example is the 'Sainte Famille' care home in Thimister-Clermont, whose entire building is covered with solar panels. The source text is limited, so further details of the arrangement are not available here.
items.interest_reason: No profile basis yet; neutral rating for a regional energy story.

items.title: EU agrees delay to methane import monitoring obligations
items.headline: EU countries agree to postpone methane monitoring and reporting duties for fossil fuel importers to 2029.
items.summary: The Council of the EU has agreed a targeted amendment to the methane regulation. It delays monitoring, reporting and verification obligations for importers of natural gas, crude oil and coal from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2029. The amendment is intended to safeguard security of supply.
items.interest_reason: No profile basis yet; neutral rating for a regulatory amendment.

items.title: Council and Parliament agree on faster grid permitting
items.headline: Council and Parliament strike deal to streamline permitting under the EU grids package.
items.summary: The Council and the European Parliament have reached an agreement on measures to streamline permitting under the grids package, aimed at a faster clean energy transition. Member states will have 1.5 years to incorporate the directive's provisions into national law.
items.interest_reason: No profile basis yet; neutral rating for a grids legislation deal.

items.title: 333 gas suppliers announce price increases from January 1
items.headline: Hundreds of German gas suppliers raise prices from 1 January as Iran war costs filter through.
items.summary: Handelsblatt has published an interactive calculator showing how much more households may pay after 333 basic supply providers announced gas price increases effective 1 January. The rises reflect high gas prices caused by the Iran war. The tool lets families estimate their own extra costs.
items.interest_reason: Energy prices affecting households; relevant to German energy market coverage

items.title: Firewood prices rise as heating costs climb
items.headline: Firewood has become more expensive, and wood-burning remains common in German homes.
items.summary: Handelsblatt reports that wood prices have risen sharply in recent years alongside the energy crisis. Fireplaces remain widespread in Germany, and the article outlines ways owners can cut costs.
items.interest_reason: Consumer heating story with limited policy or market relevance

items.title: UN climate conference in Antalya ends without joint declaration
items.headline: Antalya climate talks collapse without a final declaration over fossil fuel phase-out wording.
items.summary: Delegates at the world climate conference in Antalya failed to agree on a closing statement. The dispute centres on whether the text should refer to phasing out coal, oil and gas. The EU refused to accept a draft that omitted any reference to fossil fuels, and German Environment Minister Schneider had called the draft unacceptable.
items.interest_reason: Major climate policy outcome; directly relevant to energy and climate policy

items.title: Farmers' lobby mobilises against EU direct payment cuts
items.headline: The German Farmers' Association calls new protests against planned cuts to EU direct payments.
items.summary: The Deutscher Bauernverband is calling for fresh protests against proposed reductions in EU direct payments. An FAZ feature asks how a relatively small group has gained such influence in policy debates.
items.interest_reason: Agricultural policy, outside the energy and environment focus

items.title: Ministers warn of extra costs from German renewables reform
items.headline: German ministers warn that the renewables reform could raise costs, and the SPD objects to grid-area cuts.
items.summary: German ministers told coalition lawmakers that the planned renewables reform could create extra costs. The Social Democrats oppose reducing compensation for new wind and solar plants in grid-congested areas.
items.interest_reason: Core German renewables policy dispute within the coalition
